text_blocks.snippet: Yes, COVID-19 infection can lead to lung scarring, known as pulmonary fibrosis.
snippet_highlighted_words: Yes, COVID-19 infection can lead to lung scarring

text_blocks.snippet: The virus can damage the cells lining the lungs (alveolar epithelial cells), causing inflammation and damage. This damage can lead to the formation of scar tissue, which can thicken the walls of the alveoli (air sacs) and reduce their ability to exchange oxygen and carbon dioxide.

Lung scarring caused by COVID-19 can range from mild to severe and may take weeks, months, or even years to develop. In some cases, it can lead to chronic lung disease, such as bronchiolitis obliterans organizing pneumonia (BOOP) or idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF).
